title: Interpret response
description: What /interpret returns. Success and failure share ONE flat shape - on an error the three explanation fields are empty strings and errorCode is set. That is a concession to Unity's JsonUtility, which cannot express a discriminated union or an optional nested object: one layout means the C# client has exactly one DTO and checks exactly one field, instead of guessing which of two shapes arrived. Every 2xx, 4xx and 5xx from the Lambda matches this schema; only a failure raised by API Gateway itself (a missing API key, a body rejected by the request validator) will not, and the C# client falls back to a transport-level error there.

surfaceType.description: What the surface is as a whole, in plain language. Empty on error.

atThisPoint.description: What is happening at the clicked point specifically. Empty on error.

directionalBehavior.description: Which way the surface rises and falls from here. Empty on error.

classificationKind.description: Echoed verbatim from the request's classification.kind. This is NEVER read out of the generated text - whatever the prose says, the label the UI displays is the one Unity's own second-derivative test produced. It is the single most important guarantee in this contract.

cached.description: True when served from DynamoDB without calling the model. Useful for confirming the cache is doing its job, since Bedrock is the only usage-billed step.

modelId.description: Which model produced it. Empty on error.

promptVersion.description: Prompt version that produced the wording.

requestId.description: Lambda request id. Quote this when searching CloudWatch.

errorCode.description: Empty on success. A stable machine-readable code on failure, so the client can branch without matching on message text.

errorMessage.description: Human-readable reason, safe to show in the UI. Empty on success.
